title: Latent Diffusion — Stable Diffusion and Classifier-Free Guidance

questions.question: What do encode(x) and decode(z) do in this toy latent diffusion pipeline?
options: encode scales x by 0.5 and decode scales z by 2.0
encode adds Gaussian noise and decode applies a softmax
encode maps a scalar to a one-hot class and decode removes the class
Both functions return their input unchanged
questions.explanation: The helpers are explicit inverses: encode(x)=x*0.5 and decode(z)=z*2.0.

questions.question: Why does init_net use an input width of x_dim + t_dim + c_dim?
options: The network predicts one separate model for every class and timestep
forward concatenates the noisy latent, timestep embedding, and class embedding
The decoder receives both the original image and its decoded copy
The extra dimensions store the diffusion schedule itself
questions.explanation: forward forms `inp = x_t + t_emb + c_emb`, so W1 must accept all three pieces.

questions.question: What ID represents the dropped conditioning signal in main?
options: Class 1
Class 0
NULL_CLASS=2
The timestep T
questions.explanation: The training loop uses `use_c = NULL_CLASS if rng.random() < 0.1 else c`, with NULL_CLASS defined as 2.

questions.question: What epsilon estimate does CFG construct from conditional and unconditional predictions?
options: eps_cfg = eps_u - eps_c, independent of w
eps_cfg = w*eps_c + (1-w)*eps_u for every w
eps_cfg = eps_c / (eps_u + w)
eps_cfg = (1+w)*eps_c - w*eps_u
questions.explanation: The sampling closure explicitly extrapolates away from the unconditional estimate with `(1+w)*eps_c - w*eps_u`.

questions.question: What happens to the CFG result when w=0.0?
options: eps_cfg equals eps_c, so there is no guidance extrapolation beyond the conditional prediction
eps_cfg equals eps_u, so conditioning is fully dropped
The sampler uses a uniform random epsilon
The latent is decoded before the reverse chain starts
questions.explanation: Substituting w=0 into the formula leaves eps_c unchanged.

questions.question: Why does the model sometimes train with one_hot(NULL_CLASS, 3) instead of the true class?
options: It balances the two real classes by deleting 10% of their samples
The 10% conditioning dropout teaches an unconditional branch that CFG can query at sampling time
It prevents the timestep embedding from being computed
It makes the latent encoder invertible
questions.explanation: Classifier-free guidance needs both conditional and null-condition predictions, so the training loop deliberately drops c on a fraction of examples.
